amendments.text:
# Prospective native history path correction before physical admission

Two compiler-only failures were preserved: a FullyConnected with two inbound layers
was rejected; explicit Concatenate then reported an incompatible IP version. Neither
opened a physical device. The failed fixture folders remain fixtures01 and fixtures02.

The admitted candidate is sequential: fixed feature encoder -> one FNP3 with32
plastic context records plus8 fixed helper records -> fixed output relay. Helpers
reconstruct the eight raw-history dual-rail values from the designed conjunction
basis. Each helper has32 connections, potential8 or0, activation threshold7 and
learning threshold32. Since input potential cannot exceed32, the strict greater-than
learning eligibility rule excludes them without a context-dependent label. Verify
helper RAM is unchanged at every boundary. Plastic records retain threshold27 and
zero initial learning threshold; all40 records share class0. The last three decoded
raw symbols feed the first48 output channels, while learned responses use64:96.
One initial buffer supplies an explicit zero-valued three-symbol prior; subsequent
host writes are only16 current-symbol channels. No fork/merge or host history copy.

All other prospective stages, controls, seeds and limits remain. This is an explicit
fixed shift-register mechanism alongside unsupervised allocation, not discovered
history dynamics. Helper outputs and conjunction activations are derived from
measured inputs plus unchanged fixed weights; final output and RAM are measured.

# Stronger trained-frozen control before physical admission

Virtual qualification exposed that a one-cycle frozen prefix recognizes zero or one
history: too weak as the principal frozen comparison. Replace it prospectively.
After three unlabelled zero warmup bits and sixteen unlabelled0001-periodic bits,
train the four repeating histories with64 further0001-periodic bits. Probe them
without learning for16 bits. Native/frozen/severed share this exact training prefix;
always-unlabelled receives no labels. Require all four old histories to have distinct
single-record responses before admitting the16-history expansion. The frozen arm
then disables learning globally for the entire16-history expansion. Native/severed
continue constant-label0 learning for1,2,4,12 de Bruijn cycles. Probe two cycles as
before. Old four-history assignments must retain their exact record IDs. The final
strong frozen comparison is expected to retain its four known histories, while the
intact learner must allocate the other twelve and retain all sixteen. CPU dictionary
learns the same raw windows with the same teaching schedule; it must also succeed.
All other source/hardware gates remain. Forward count131+16*cycles per session.

# CPU admission verifier repair before hardware

First CPU-only one-cycle trace matched saved inputs, outputs, full RAM, potentials
and raw-symbol dictionary, but the audit prematurely required the final16-history
CPU endpoint at the one-cycle prefix. Transition windows from the old periodic
stream mean that endpoint belongs to the frozen12-cycle gate. Restrict that single
endpoint assertion to12 cycles, as intended in the original staged protocol. No
native fixture or circuit changes. Preserve cpu_s113101_native_c1 as a failed audit;
refreeze and rerun under an attempt suffix before any hardware admission.

# One-class no-label semantics found on hardware; explicit query mode gate

The first physical session stopped after its first unlabelled warmup forward.
Output/input matched, but full RAM showed one native connection edit (record3,
score8, sixteen->fourteen swap budget). In a one-class bank, omitted teacher label
with global learning enabled did not make the call read-only. This differs from
our earlier multi-class query protocol. Preserve the entire one-forward failure.
No claim about the undocumented internal mode mechanism is made from this alone.

Prospective correction: globally disable learning for every scheduled query/warmup
forward, enable only constant-label0 training forwards. Save the requested mode
sequence in addition to descriptors and raw RAM. Full per-event RAM replay and
fixed-helper invariance must still pass; this amendment does not waive any gate.
Mode toggles and diagnostic RAM reads are host work. No claim of autonomous learning
phase selection. Refreeze corrected source/binary; rerun seed113101 native1 under a
new attempt suffix before any later stage. Additional hidden-state mismatch must
stop again and be investigated rather than silently changing the reference.

# Learning-mode-specific CPU accumulator correction

The explicitly gated suffix failed at its first training event19. All preceding
19 outputs and RAM states matched. The first native edit is compatible with initial
selector rotor0 (also31 for this one edit), while the CPU that had accumulated query
scores predicted21. Queries with globally disabled learning need a distinct CPU
transition from the earlier multi-class no-label/global-enabled calls. The corrected
CPU leaves its learning selector accumulator unchanged during disabled forwards.
This is a behavioral reference hypothesis, not a read of that hidden register. It
must qualify against the entire hardware trace, including training-query-training
transitions; no gate is waived. Preserve native_s113101_native_c1_attempt2 and the
old fixtures04. Fresh compiler/reference fixtures05 and a new frozen binary/source
are required. No weights, feature basis, labels, stream or scientific endpoint change.

# Prospective unseen-order retention suffix after all five main seeds pass

All19 main physical sessions passed (plus two preserved early failed hardware
prefixes). Before interpreting learned context as more than a memorized traversal,
append128 unlabelled raw bits generated once by NumPy PCG64 seed113901. This suffix
has all16 four-bit histories in a new order. It is not supplied a history ID or
teacher label. Existing323-event native12 prefix stays byte-identical; no program,
RAM, threshold or native history reset at the suffix. Require one correct original
record ID for every held-out window and completely unchanged connection/helper RAM.
The strong raw-symbol CPU dictionary must also succeed. Query learning stays disabled.

New separate runs: native+suffix for each of five fixed initializations; matched
trained-frozen+suffix for seed113101 (retains only its four learned histories).
Admit the first new native suffix, inspect, then frozen suffix, inspect, then the
other four native suffixes. Keep original runs/fixtures and append new plan files.
New arm names unseen and unseen_frozen. Each has451 events. Existing session/forward
caps still suffice:25 qualified +2 failed admissions <=28; all work before existing
cutoff. No outcome prediction, latent-world discovery or performance claim added.

# Held-out CPU receipt serialization repair before new physical suffix

The held-out CPU trace passed every array and endpoint assertion, but writing its
AUDIT.json failed because a summed NumPy boolean became a non-JSON int64. Preserve
cpu_s113101_unseen_c12 and its arrays/receipt as a failed audit. Convert the summed
booleans to Python int, refreeze, and rerun CPU under a new suffix. No native program,
fixture, learning/reference behavior or scientific endpoint changes. No physical
held-out session had been admitted at this failure.
